feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications/platform leadership, with clear domain focus and solid progression at NACo. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat dense, repetitive across sections, and could sharpen impact by emphasizing outcomes over responsibilities.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently support a strong niche in public-sector digital platforms, governance, analytics, and content operations.  
- Credibility and progression: long tenure at one organization with visible advancement from coordinator to director strengthens trust and leadership narrative.  
- Good use of scale indicators: metrics like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” add substance.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more measurable outcomes: several bullets describe duties (“led,” “advised,” “developed”) without showing business/user impact, efficiency gains, engagement lifts, or adoption results.  
- Minor style/consistency issues: mixed punctuation/list style, inconsistent use of commas in series (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs other lines), and slightly promotional phrasing in Education (“Ranked among the top public universities...”). No major misspellings or grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly broad and repeats themes covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and make it more outcome-oriented: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years driving web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with more active leadership language such as “leading” or “scaling” to better match director-level experience.
- Consider trimming the list to 3–4 core strengths most relevant to target roles: web modernization, governance/editorial systems, analytics infrastructure, and AI-enabled content/search experiences.
- Optional rewrite: “Senior digital platform leader with 12+ years leading web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Delivers scalable editorial systems, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Senior digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle; vary the phrasing.
- The long capability list duplicates Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. It would be stronger if it emphasized higher-level capability areas and used tighter, more parallel phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, category-style phrases with consistent structure; e.g.: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and optimization • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Replace “content experiences” with “content discovery” for clearer meaning and stronger alignment with the AI search project.
- Change “operations” to “leadership” where appropriate to better reflect seniority, especially for communications and governance.
- Standardize style by using “and” instead of “&” if the rest of the CV favors a more formal tone.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; consider trimming to 6 items or making it more strategic than technical.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” also overlaps with the dedicated Multimedia/Technical sections.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the block largely repeats themes already covered in Work Experience and skills. It would be stronger with tighter formatting, clearer outcomes, and more distinct project framing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected Recent Projects” framing to reinforce recency and distinguish this from core experience.
- Tighten wording and standardize parallel structure: start each item with a strong verb and keep lists concise.
- Where possible, add one concrete outcome or scope marker per project (audience, usage, campaign purpose, or scale).
- Revise for style consistency: use “10 x 20-foot” instead of “10×20-foot,” and consider “AI-powered” or “AI-enabled” consistently across the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series closely overlap with the current freelance role and NACo bullets.
- The anniversary campaign may add the most unique value because it introduces archival storytelling and conference display work not emphasized elsewhere.

items.title: Coleman Davis
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project section. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact contributions and add outcomes or scale.

Suggested edit
- Open with impact + client context: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, and communications systems improvement.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into sharper outcomes: combine digital systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one bullet focused on enterprise communications operations.
- Make technical bullets more results-oriented: “Built Drupal campaign microsites, modular storytelling components, and member toolkits” plus any metrics (launches, users, engagement, publishing speed, reduced support tickets).
- Rephrase AI work to show leadership and novelty: “Led AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content model, and discovery UX for complex policy/member content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, enterprise web improvement” repeats the summary and NACo role; keep only what is new in this engagement.
- Footer projects already cover microsite and AI search details, so this item should emphasize leadership, scope, and outcomes rather than feature lists.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact role with good scale metrics, but it reads a bit like a responsibility list. Tighten around 3–4 signature outcomes and make leadership/business impact more explicit.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to emphasize outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where missing: for analytics, governance, and studio build, note reporting speed, production cost/time savings, audience growth, or increased internal publishing efficiency if available.
- Consolidate channel management: combine email/social into one concise bullet and specify scale only once.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Video leadership overlaps with the earlier NACo roles and footer project list; focus here on building the in-house studio and organizational capacity, not recurring video production.
- Governance/editorial coordination also appears in prior NACo roles; position this entry as enterprise-level standardization and cross-department operating model.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize what he owned at this level versus broader leadership/platform work later.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to stress operational ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, supporting advocacy messaging and cross-team editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground scale: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video contribution with outcome language: “Produced and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper point: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing coordination and consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” is too close to the Director role’s channel oversight; use “managed” or “ran” instead of “led.”
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling/formalizing the series, not launching it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it largely repeats the header and Core Competencies. Make it sharper, more senior, and more distinct by emphasizing governance, enterprise scale, and audience outcomes rather than generic communications phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Replace with tighter, less overlapping bullets:
- Enterprise digital strategy and web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership for complex organizations
- Public-sector, membership, and advocacy content strategy
- Audience-centered planning, usability, and content discovery
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “content strategy” or “communications strategy” to sound more senior and operational.
- If space allows elsewhere, connect this area to scale/results already proven in experience: 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” overlaps with several work-experience bullets on storytelling, usability, and editorial coordination.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes, not repeat every specific technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms (WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages) • CMS modernization and front-end implementation • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Remove lower-signal basics like “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” from this section; keep them in Technical + IT.
- Put the strongest, most recent differentiators first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “Enterprise CMS modernization for high-volume public-facing sites” to echo the 10,000+ page migration experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search experiences” duplicates Core Competencies and Recent Projects; keep wording consistent but avoid repeating it too prominently.
- Most platform/tool names are already listed in Technical + IT, so this section should stay more strategic than exhaustive.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section and reads more like a tool dump than a senior-value summary. Make it more outcome-oriented and leadership-level.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization” rather than a pure software list.
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” + “KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Consider stronger phrasing: replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboarding and decision support.”
- If space allows elsewhere, add measurable context tied to recent work, such as supporting reporting for a 10,000+ page site or 3.5M annual page views.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is highly duplicative of “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep one tools-heavy version and make this one more strategic.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with broader “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus multiple work-experience bullets. Make it more senior, operational, and outcomes-oriented rather than listing basic tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something broader and more leadership-level, e.g. **Multimedia Production, Studio Operations & Event Delivery**
- Tighten and elevate phrasing: **Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event production workflows**
- If space allows, add scope/impact language instead of tools alone: **In-house studio buildout, recurring advocacy video programming, and live event production**
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with **Video strategy, production and post-production** to better reflect leadership, not just execution

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the Core Competencies line **“Multimedia production and livestream operations.”** Differentiate by emphasizing studio systems/event delivery here.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” and “Livestreaming” are close; combine to avoid repetition.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” section. This item should either be tightened or reframed to emphasize depth in the most relevant platforms, especially Drupal.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize by relevance/recency: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add light proficiency cues: “Drupal (advanced) • WordPress (working) • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- Consider renaming to “CMS & Web Platforms” for cleaner phrasing and consistency with the rest of the CV.
- If you want more impact, swap GitHub Pages for a higher-value qualifier on Drupal rather than listing five tools equally.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills; keep one version more strategic and this one more tool-focused.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid over-listing it elsewhere without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and slightly more current/senior.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from languages/tools to applied capability: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag implementation • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Consider replacing “Google Tag Manager” with “tag implementation / GTM” so it reads as a capability, not just a tool.
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier tied to recent work: “Drupal front-end implementation” or “CMS technical troubleshooting” to connect with current consulting work.
- Keep only the strongest, current items; if jQuery is not actively used, move it later or drop it.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- GTM may also overlap with “Data, Analytics & Optimization”; decide whether it belongs there instead.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too long and mixes automation platforms with collaboration/project-management tools. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit
- Split by function and lead with true automation tools: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier” first; move Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello to a separate “Project & Work Management” line if space allows.
- Tighten phrasing to emphasize application, e.g. rename to: “Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools.”
- If you want more impact, add a brief qualifier instead of a pure list: “Built workflow automations and editorial coordination systems using Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier; managed team operations in Jira, Asana, and Trello.”
- Consider dropping 1–2 lower-value/general tools (Slack, Teams, Basecamp) unless they are specifically important for target roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills.
- Slack/Teams are generic workplace tools and add little differentiation.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this line is too bare to add much value on its own. It should signal level of use and align with the CV’s stronger story around enterprise communications operations.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (enterprise email campaigns, newsletter operations, audience segmentation)
- If accurate, add scale/context in parentheses: “used for member communications, campaign sends, and automated journeys”
- Keep only the strongest/current platforms; if one was lightly used, remove it rather than listing every tool

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This already overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” and multiple work-experience bullets about email/newsletters; avoid repeating generic email capability elsewhere
- If Dynamics 365 or Higher Logic were central in recent roles, consider reflecting that in a recent experience bullet instead of relying only on this skills line

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and the NACo director bullet about expanding analytics infrastructure. Use this space to sharpen the technical stack and methods, not broad capability labels.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: “GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI/dashboard design”
- Swap “SEO” for “Google Search Console” or “technical SEO” to make it more concrete and tool/discipline-specific.
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “KPI/dashboard design” or “reporting architecture” to sound more senior and outcome-oriented.
- If space allows, order by strongest/recent tools first: “GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity …”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates the “Topline Skills” analytics section; consider trimming one of the two or making this version more tool-specific.
- “A/B testing” may feel unsupported unless referenced elsewhere in experience; keep only if you’ve used it directly.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational: emphasize team-building, early systems/process work, and any concrete production scale or platform outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to focus on “built/established” impact: “Promoted across two digital roles; helped establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add 1–2 measurable outcomes if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, cadence of weekly videos, audience growth, or turnaround improvements.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce soft terms like “high-impact” and “major”; replace with specifics.
- Suggested version: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported a website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped standardize cross-channel publishing workflows across web, email, social and multimedia. Provided day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/establishing the format, not expanding it.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow/governance language already used more strongly in later NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads broadly and undersells the most distinctive achievement. Since later NACo roles already cover digital leadership, this item should emphasize foundational innovation/program support and the first-podcast launch.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams; launched the organization’s first podcast from concept through scripting and production.”
- Trim generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a sharper verb/result, e.g., “produced digital and multimedia content to support member-facing communications.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders served.
- Consider a two-part structure: first clause on innovation/research coordination, second on podcast/content production.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad multimedia language already covered in later NACo roles (video, digital content, channel operations).
- Don’t overstate digital leadership here; later positions show the progression more credibly.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads a bit generic and overlaps with stronger multimedia claims already established in recent roles. Tighten it toward tools/software and use more specific production terminology.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Broadcast/livestream studio production • Podcast recording, editing & production”
- Keep naming conventions consistent with other technical sections by using product names rather than mixed tools + workflow phrases.
- Replace “Livestream studio workflows” with a clearer capability phrase like “Broadcast/livestream studio production” or “Studio and hybrid event production.”
